decisions.text: type bar: categories compared by value
clustered bars: 2 series of one measure across categories (G1.56, R9-12)
nominal categories sorted by value, descending (by series dom)
2 series side by side in each cluster, the bars touching, in the same order in every cluster: Domestic (slot 1), International (slot 2) (G7.5, G4.22)
“Guitars” and “Drums” come within 10 pt of each other under vertical bars, with every multi-word name wrapped: horizontal bars, names right-aligned at the left
labels as a set, 1 decimals, bare numbers: 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0
digits hidden: millions, stated in the scale's title (R2-05, D-3): “Sales ($ million)”
a horizontal scale: bare numbers, and its title centred below with the unit in parentheses: “Sales ($ million)”
the colours of a cluster run top to bottom: each series named beside its bar of the last cluster, in the order of the bars (G5.1, D-31 (c))

source.shows: the book's data the other way round: the ten product lines as the categories and the two markets as the series, so two colours instead of ten; the names do not fit under columns, so the clusters turn, and their colours, running top to bottom, are named beside the bars of the last cluster (D-31 (c))
